# AGENTS.md generated by Atlas

Atlas memory is canonical. This file is a short provider projection, not the source of truth.
Regenerate with `atlas memory projection --target=agents --write` after Atlas memory changes.

## Operating Contract
- Use the Atlas memory registry and Context Pack as canonical context.
- Treat this file as a compact bootstrap for external tools.
- Do not expose Atlas internal IDs, traces, prompts or provider details unless the operator asks for audit.
- If context is missing or stale, ask Atlas for fresh context instead of inventing facts.

## Provider-Safe Memory
- [decision][global] Atlas owns canonical memory: Atlas memory is canonical; provider files are generated projections, not the source of truth.
- [technical_context][global] Provider projections must contain provider-safe memory: A managed provider projection with zero provider-safe memory is not ready for real Claude/Codex work.
- [technical_context][global] Atlas server requires Homebrew PHP 8.4+: Use /opt/homebrew/bin/php for Artisan and Composer workflows in atlas-server.
- [decision][global] Keep external memory infrastructure explicit: Local hybrid recall and audited Open Brain context export are implemented; ChromaDB, MCP remote and multiuser sync still require explicit phase and DoD.
- [harness_learning][global] Sync docs and code intelligence after memory changes: After changing canonical docs or code, run engineering knowledge sync and index-code before relying on context packs.
- [decision][global] Migrations: nunca INSERT INTO migrations manualmente: Migrations devem ser idempotentes; nunca carimbar manualmente o registro.
- [decision][global] Database em dev: fresh > reparo: DB local que diverge = nuke + recreate, não migration de reparo.
- [technical_context][global] Invariantes de schema vivem no DB, não no ORM: Invariantes mecânicos (updated_at, CHECK, FK, defaults) vivem no DB; lógica de negócio no código.
- [decision][global] Profiles are domain operating systems, not model presets: Atlas domain/flow profiles must define complete orchestration systems: models, providers, orchestrators, runtimes, skills, memory, gates, autonomy, evidence, fallback, background policy and learning loop.
- [technical_context][global] Programming policy context is projected through chat gateway and worker: AiChatCommand, AiGatewayService and AiWorker now preserve programming profile context and execution policy as auditable programming fields.
- [technical_context][global] Programming orchestrator consumes execution_policy for executor selection: AtlasProgrammingOrchestrator now uses AtlasAiPolicyService execution_policy as the executor authority for dev, complete dev and forge flows.
- [technical_context][global] Atlas AI policy exposes execution_policy/profile_context: AtlasAiPolicyService now exposes explicit execution policy and profile context for app/CLI/background consumers.
- [technical_context][global] Engineering Harness patch artifacts expose integrity packet: Harness run payloads now include patch_artifacts.*.integrity with checked, exists, hash_matches and sha256/reason for persisted diff evidence.
- [technical_context][global] programming_completion.repair summarizes native repair loops: Native dev_repair_executor completions now expose repair iteration state, stop reason, quality statuses, and compact history.
- [technical_context][global] Native dev_repair_executor enforces quality-worsening stop: AiWorker now honors stop_when_quality_worsens for native provider repair loops and stops instead of enqueueing another repair when quality regresses.
- [technical_context][global] Native dev_repair_executor runs in AiWorker provider path: AiWorker now executes non-Harness dev_repair_executor repair loops after provider success using AtlasCliQualityService and same-trace repair jobs.
- [technical_context][global] Atlas programming repair is orchestrator-owned: AtlasProgrammingOrchestrator owns programming_repair and repair prompt generation for dev_repair_executor flows.

## Manual Notes

### Atlas MCP: consultar ANTES de implementar

**Antes de qualquer mudança de código, recomendação técnica ou resposta sobre arquitetura neste projeto, chamar pelo menos UMA tool do MCP `atlas-open-brain`.** Não é opcional.

| Quando | Tool |
|---|---|
| Pergunta toca decisão, regra, learning ou padrão já catalogado | `atlas_memory_recall` |
| Vai começar feature nova ou refator que toca múltiplos módulos | `atlas_open_brain_context_pack` |
| Suspeita que o índice está stale ou drift entre projection e código | `atlas_memory_maintenance_status` |

**Não confiar** em memória do treino, em `grep` cego no código, ou na seção `Provider-Safe Memory` acima — ela é foto fixa que envelhece. Atlas é a fonte viva.

**Por que essa regra é imperativa, não descritiva:** o `Operating Contract` acima diz "use Atlas as canonical context", mas em sessões longas o modelo esquece e cai no atalho do grep. Resultado: implementação que ignora decisão já tomada, vira refator depois. Atlas indexa ~22 docs, ~8.700 símbolos, decisões auditadas — pular consulta = reinventar contexto que já existe. Custo de chamada: ~1s. Custo de divergir: horas.

**Exceções legítimas** (não precisa consultar):
- Renomear variável dentro de uma função
- Fix de typo, ajuste de whitespace, formatação
- Tarefa puramente operacional (rodar comando, ler log)
- Resposta de pergunta sobre o próprio Atlas/MCP/ferramental (meta)

Se em dúvida se a tarefa cai em exceção: **não cai. Consulta.**
